title: The comfort of hierarchy
heading: Beyond the Hierarchy
objective: Recognize a phrase inside a line inside a stanza.
action: Three labelled enclosures settle around the poem, the first line and its opening phrase.

captions.text: Some structures fit neatly inside others.

narration.text: The moon rose slowly above the sleeping sea. Two lines make a stanza.

title: Another way of reading
heading: Reading the poem
objective: Find where a poetic line ends and a predicate continues.
action: Mark the two poetic lines. Show the subject, the continuing predicate and its prepositional phrase. Bring the line marks back.

captions.text: What the moon did spans both lines.
A text can have more than one structure.

narration.text: The predicate starts with “rose” and continues across the line break.

title: The collision
heading: Where the boundaries fall
objective: Trace why the line and predicate cannot each be one whole element in the same nested tree.
action: Open the poem into a single sequence. Fit enclosures to the line and predicate. Trace their four boundaries in reading order.

captions.text: What happens when their boundaries cross?

narration.text: The line opens first. The predicate begins inside it, but ends outside it.

title: Liberation from the tree
heading: From containers to tracks
objective: Follow the same four endpoints as the enclosures flatten into independent tracks.
action: Fold the upper edges onto the lower edges. Lower the strokes onto separate tracks while endpoint guides remain attached to the first and last character Cells.

narration.text: Keep the boundary characters in view. Each enclosure folds into its own track, and both ranges stay whole.

title: Freedom of arrangement
heading: Two independent ranges
objective: Distinguish disjoint, nested, coincident and crossing ranges.
action: Glide the same pair of tracks between four arrangements. Name each once its endpoints settle.

narration.text: One range can nest inside another.
Crossing ranges overlap at one end.

title: Beyond a single ontology
heading: Systems of description
objective: See different kinds of concepts and relationships at work on the same passage.
action: Return to verse. Add line divisions, grammatical roles and a rhetorical figure one system at a time. Match each mark to its example below the poem.

captions.text: Annotations need not share a hierarchy.
Nor need they share an ontology.

narration.text: Poetics marks the lines. Grammar pairs a subject with its predicate. Rhetoric reads a sleeping sea as personification. Each system brings its own concepts.

title: The arrival of a new ontology
heading: A new way in
objective: Watch a literary system arrive independently of the three established systems.
action: Keep the poem and its three rows fixed. Add a diamond-ended literary range and a fourth row relating imagery to atmosphere.

captions.text: Nothing else needs to be dismantled.

narration.text: A literary reading adds atmosphere. The other three systems stay in place.

title: Beyond a single interpretation
heading: Two readings of one image
objective: Recognize two attributed readings with identical textual boundaries.
action: Isolate the sleeping sea in the verse. Two equal tracks span the same phrase and lead to separately attributed readings.

narration.text: One reader hears tranquillity. Another senses power waiting to wake. Both point to the same words.

title: Synthesis
heading: One shared passage
objective: See hierarchy, independent systems and open interpretations together.
action: Restore the whole poem and all four systems. The literary entry carries both readings side by side.

narration.text: The stanza and both readings can stand together.

title: Many ways of knowing
objective: Recall the progression from one text to many systems of knowledge.
action: Reveal the closing lines in sequence on the engraved series card. Pause before the final line and hold the series identifier.

narration.text: One text. Many structures. Many ontologies.
